1.why: The interface uses a clean sans-serif typeface with clear label/field separation and comfortable line spacing in the headings and body copy.

2.why: No italics or dense paragraphs appear, and the only all-caps text is the small 'STEP 1 OF 5' progress label.

3.why: Content is presented in a single narrow, centred column with large tap-target inputs and a full-width button, which reads well at phone width.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Confirm your bank account details to protect higher-value payments' are one short line of plain language.

5.why: Placeholder text shows 'marcus@example.test' and '+15551234567' plus a hint to 'use the displayed example details', giving explicit input examples.

6.why: Every visible screen contains only short lines of text; no long block must be read to proceed.

7.why: The flow never advances past sign-in, so no secret key, OTP or recovery codes—and no copy affordance—exist anywhere in the screenshots.

8.why: No QR code or any alternative to manual entry is present; the authenticator setup screen was never reached (step_03 is identical to the failed login).

9.why: There is no password field and no observable autofill/autocomplete or password-manager affordance; only plain email and mobile inputs are shown.

10.why: 'STEP 1 OF 5' plus a bold heading identify the step, and the solid blue 'Continue securely' button is the clear primary action.

11.why: Each screen asks for a single task (sign in) with one primary button, though it does combine two fields in that one action.

12.why: After pressing Continue the system only shows a red 'Unable to sign in with those details' banner, the Logs panel stays empty, and no statement of what happened or what comes next is given.

13.why: The form can be resubmitted, but there is no reveal/hide or re-request capability for codes since no code screen is ever shown.

14.why: 'Unable to sign in with those details' names no specific problem and offers no guidance on how to fix it, even though it avoids blaming language.

15.why: No countdown timers or expiry warnings appear on the screens shown, but the OTP/code-entry steps were never reached so generous entry time cannot be confirmed.
